A type parameter relates two things: an argument to the return type, or one argument to another. One that appears only once relates nothing. Write its constraint, or `unknown`, in its place and the signature means the same.

A type parameter that appears only as the return type is worse. The caller picks any type and the compiler believes it, which is a type assertion in disguise.

The rule checks functions, methods and classes. Uses inside a function body do not count, only the signature.

This rule needs type information. Run `bun lint --type-aware`.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 3} */}
```ts
function log<Message>(message: Message): void {
  console.log(message);
}

function size<Item extends { length: number }>(item: Item): number {
  return item.length;
}

function load<Data>(key: string): Data {
  return JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(key) ?? "null");
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
function log(message: unknown): void {
  console.log(message);
}

function size(item: { length: number }): number {
  return item.length;
}

function load(key: string): unknown {
  return JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(key) ?? "null");
}
```

Here each type parameter ties two places together:

{/* good */}
```ts
function first<Item>(items: Item[]): Item | undefined {
  return items[0];
}

function pick<Source, Key extends keyof Source>(source: Source, key: Key) {
  return source[key];
}

class Box<Value> {
  constructor(private value: Value) {}

  get(): Value {
    return this.value;
  }
}
```
